newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bans police from drinking on the job.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bans police from drinking on the job.

text.p: China's Shanghai city has banned its policemen from drinking alcohol on the job and from getting drunk at any time, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Monday.
The city's police department has issued an order aimed at maintaining the good image of the force, banning drinking during working hours, including at lunch time, the newspaper said.
Officers cannot drink when they are carrying arms or secret documents, driving cars or if they are wearing uniforms in public places, it said.
They are not allowed to accept drinks from people when they are dealing with cases, from anyone who might influence them in their work or from criminals, it said.
When officers are drinking with guests, they must not display "uncivilised" behaviour and must not get drunk at any time or any place, it said but gave no more details.

The ban appeared to be aimed at curbing drinking by police officials at dinners given by people eager to improve their relations with the police. Liquor is also a popular gift to officials, especially at festivals.
